title: Prompt Shields spend budgets (budget.v1)
description: Spend budgets shared by the SDK (ShieldsRouter, the plain clients) and the gateway. A budget caps the USD spend of one attribution subject (business unit, use case, owner, or everything) per UTC day, ISO week or calendar month. Spend counters live in a BudgetStore under the key format in schemas/budget/README.md, so every enforcement point that shares a store and a namespace shares the counters. Cross-field rules JSON Schema cannot express: budget ids are unique; a 'global' budget has no subject; every other scope needs one.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editors.

namespace.description: Counter namespace (the key's second segment). Enforcement points that must share spend use the same namespace and the same store; a multi-tenant store uses one namespace per tenant.

on_store_error.description: What happens when the store cannot be read. 'open' (default): the call goes ahead unchanged and budget_state is 'unknown'. 'closed': block budgets refuse the call and downgrade budgets downgrade it as if exhausted. Warn budgets never change a call. Recording spend after a call never fails it.

id.description: Unique id, reported as budget_id in telemetry.

scope.description: The attribution attribute the budget is keyed on: business_unit (X-PS-Business-Unit), use_case (X-PS-Use-Case), owner (X-PS-Owner; use it for team budgets), or global (every call).

subject.description: The attribute value the budget applies to, compared exactly. '*' applies the budget to every value separately (one counter per value). Calls without the attribute never match a non-global budget.

window.description: UTC calendar window: day (00:00 UTC), ISO week (Monday 00:00 UTC), calendar month.

mode.description: warn: never changes a call. downgrade: routers clamp each call's estimated cost to the remaining budget within the route policy's constraints (the max_cost clamp); once exhausted, the cheapest allowed candidate. A plain client, which does not route, switches to downgrade_model once the budget is exhausted. block: once exhausted, calls are refused before anything is sent.

warn_at.description: Fraction of limit_usd from which budget_state is 'warn'.

downgrade_model.description: mode 'downgrade' only: the model a plain (non-routing) client uses once the budget is exhausted, only when that client opts in with allow_budget_downgrade=True (the switch is not checked against any data policy). Routers ignore it. Without it, a plain client cannot downgrade and serves the call unchanged.
